transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m just not sleeping right anymore. I work overnights, so I’m used to my sleep being kind of backwards, but this is different. I’ll get off a shift feeling like I should be exhausted, like my body is heavy and I need to crash, and then I lie down and I’m just wide awake. I’ll be staring at the ceiling, turning over and over, and it feels like my mind won’t shut off even though I’m so tired.

And then when I finally do drift off, it doesn’t feel like real sleep. I keep waking up scared, like startled awake, and I don’t even feel rested after. It’s like I’m sleeping in little broken pieces, and then I wake up feeling like I never slept at all. It’s been wearing me down, and I didn’t really know what else to do, so… I came in.
Have you experienced anything particularly stressful or traumatic recently?

I don’t know… I mean, not one big thing that I can point to and say, “That’s when it started,” if that’s what you mean. Nothing like an accident or somebody attacking me or anything like that.

I’ve been trying to think about it because people keep asking, like, “Did something happen?” and I feel bad because I don’t have a good answer. My life has stress, sure, but it’s more just regular stuff piled up, I guess. Work can be a lot, especially doing overnights and taking care of people when you’re already tired, but I wouldn’t call it one specific traumatic thing recently. It’s more like… I don’t know, everything just started feeling heavier, and then the sleep got worse.
Do you have any recurring nightmares or disturbing dreams?

Yeah… I don’t know if I’d call them nightmares exactly, because I don’t always remember a whole dream like a movie or anything. It’s more like I’ll finally drift off after lying there forever, and then I wake up scared, like my body jolts awake before my brain even catches up. Sometimes I’m not even sure what I was dreaming about, I just wake up with that awful feeling, like something bad was happening or about to happen.

It’s been happening enough that sleep doesn’t feel like sleep anymore. I get off an overnight shift and I should be exhausted, and I am exhausted, but I’ll still lie there wide awake for so long. Then when I do sleep, it’s all broken up, and I wake up scared, and by the time I’m supposed to get up, I feel like I never rested at all. So… maybe they’re disturbing dreams, or maybe it’s just waking up scared, but either way it’s really wearing me down.
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're awake, outside of the times when you're trying to sleep?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t think of myself as anxious all day, if that makes sense. I get stressed like anybody, especially with work and trying to function when I’m tired, but I don’t know that I’m walking around feeling panicky or anything.

It’s more noticeable when I’m trying to sleep, or when I start thinking about whether I’m going to be able to sleep. During the day, or when I’m awake and doing things, I guess I can feel tense sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety or just being worn down. I haven’t really paid attention to it that way. So… maybe a little on edge at times, but I wouldn’t know how to separate it from being exhausted.
Do you ever find yourself reliving or re-experiencing a moment from your past as if it were happening again?

I don’t think so… not in the way people describe it, like suddenly being back there and seeing it all again. I don’t really have a moment like that that comes back. At least not that I can name.

Sometimes I get stuck thinking about things, like going over stuff in my head or feeling bad about things that happened, but it doesn’t feel like I’m actually there again. It’s more just thoughts, or feelings, or me trying to figure out why I feel the way I do. I don’t get, like, pictures taking over or anything where I lose track of where I am.

I guess if you mean do I have memories that bother me, maybe sometimes, but not like reliving something. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right. I just don’t think that happens to me.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain things, places, or activities because they make you feel uncomfortable or remind you of something unpleasant?

I don’t think so… not really in a clear way. I mean, I avoid things sometimes, but I think it’s more because I’m tired or I don’t feel up to dealing with people, not because a place reminds me of something specific.

Like, if I don’t go somewhere, it’s usually because it feels like too much effort, or I’m worried I won’t have the energy to get through it, or I just don’t want to be around noise and conversation. But I can’t think of a certain place or activity where I’m like, “I can’t go there because it brings something back.” It’s not like that.

There are things that make me uncomfortable, sure, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I haven’t noticed myself avoiding a particular street, or a certain kind of room, or people because of some memory. If I’m avoiding anything, it’s more just… life, I guess. But not because it reminds me of something unpleasant, at least not that I’m aware of.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in a safe environment?

I don’t think so… not constantly. I mean, I notice things around me sometimes, like if someone is acting weird or if I’m walking somewhere and it feels uncomfortable, but I don’t think I’m always scanning for danger, if that’s what you mean.

Most of the time when I’m in a safe place, I don’t feel like something bad is about to happen from outside, exactly. I might feel uneasy or tense sometimes, but I can’t say I’m watching doors or checking every sound or looking for threats all the time. It’s more like I’m in my head, or I’m just tired and trying to get through whatever I’m doing.

I guess I do pay attention if I’m alone somewhere or if it’s late, but that feels kind of normal to me. I wouldn’t say I’m on guard all the time in places I know are safe. At least I haven’t noticed that about myself.
Are there things you used to enjoy doing or places you used to go that you no longer do or visit because of how you've been feeling lately?

Yeah… yes. That’s actually been one of the bigger things, I think. I used to have more of a routine outside of just work and going home, and now it feels like everything has kind of narrowed down to just trying to make it through the day.

I used to go to church more, and that used to feel like something that kept me connected to people. I wasn’t always super involved every single week, but I went, and I knew people there, and it felt like a place I could show up. Lately I just… I don’t go. It feels like too much to get myself together and be around everyone, and then I feel bad because I know people probably notice, or maybe they don’t, I don’t know. But I’ve pulled back from that.

And Zumba too. I used to like that, even if I wasn’t great at it. It was something fun, something where I could move around and not think so much. But I haven’t been going. I tell myself I’m too tired, or I’ll go next time, but then next time comes and I still don’t. It just feels impossible to add anything extra when I’m already barely handling work.

I was mentoring too, and I’ve backed away from that. That one makes me feel really guilty, because it’s not just me missing a class or something. It’s like I was supposed to be there for somebody, and now I can barely be there for myself. I just get home and I’m done. I don’t have anything left in me.

Even work has gotten hard in a way that scares me, because I’m a personal care aide, so I have to be present and careful with people. And lately I can’t keep up with my care visits the way I should. I don’t feel like I can do them safely anymore sometimes. My supervisor actually had to stop me during a care-plan visit because I got so overwhelmed and stuck that I couldn’t finish it. I was just standing there, or trying to push through, but I couldn’t get my thoughts together enough to do what I was supposed to do.

So… yeah, it’s not just that I stopped doing fun things. It feels like I’ve stopped everything except the bare minimum, and even the bare minimum is starting to feel like too much.
Do you often feel guilty or ashamed about things you've done or haven't done?

Yes… all the time. It’s like my mind won’t leave it alone. I keep going back over every little thing I’ve done wrong, or think I did wrong, even small things that maybe other people wouldn’t even remember. With patients, especially, I’ll think, did I miss something, did I say the wrong thing, did I not protect them the way I should have, did I rush, did I fail them somehow. And then I’ll replay it over and over until it feels bigger and bigger.

And with my family too. I think about all the ways I haven’t been there enough, or how I should have done more, or been stronger, or paid better attention. It doesn’t really stop at one mistake. It turns into this feeling like maybe I’m just… not good. Like I’m a worthless aide, and not really useful to anybody.

And I feel ashamed saying that because I know people might tell me I’m being too hard on myself, but it doesn’t feel that way inside. It feels true when I’m thinking it. Like God is mad at me too, like I didn’t protect people better, like I was supposed to do more and I failed. I keep asking myself why I couldn’t just do things right. It’s exhausting, but I can’t seem to let it go.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track, like I haven’t weighed myself regularly or anything. My clothes… I don’t know, they maybe feel about the same? I haven’t noticed anything really dramatic where I’d say, “Oh, I lost a lot,” or “I gained a lot.”

I guess with how things have been, I’m not paying close attention to my body like that. I just kind of get dressed and try to get through the day. So if there has been a change, I don’t know that I could say for sure. Nothing obvious that I’ve noticed, though.
Is there something specific that you think might have triggered your sleep problems, even if it doesn't feel directly related to a traumatic event?

I don’t know if there was one specific thing that set it off. It’s not like I can point to one night and say, “That’s when it started,” or like it was because of one clear traumatic thing. It just… my sleep got broken up, and now it feels like I can’t get it back to normal.

A lot of it happens after my overnight shifts. I’ll get off work exhausted, like my body should just shut down, but then I get home and I’m lying there wide awake. I’ll be tired, but my mind won’t settle, and I’ll just stare or turn over and over. Then if I finally do drift off, it doesn’t feel peaceful. I wake up scared sometimes, like my body is already on alert before I even know why. And then after that I don’t feel rested at all, even if technically I slept some.

That’s honestly part of why I came in, because it’s not just “I had a bad night of sleep.” It’s like my sleep doesn’t work right anymore. I’m either awake when I should be sleeping, or I’m waking up frightened, or I get up feeling like I never really rested in the first place. So I don’t know what triggered it exactly… I just know it’s been happening and it’s wearing me down.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself from somewhere else?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying, I don’t think. Like, I’ve heard people describe that as watching themselves from above or feeling like they’re not in their own body, and I can’t really say that’s happened to me.

Sometimes I feel kind of distant or not fully present, especially when I’m worn down, but I still feel like I’m me, inside my own body. I’m not looking at myself from somewhere else. It’s more like I’m tired or foggy and trying to get through the moment, if that makes sense. But no, I don’t think I’ve had that outside-my-body feeling.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're a burden to others?

Yeah… I do. A lot. Probably more than I want to admit.

It’s like my mind just keeps going back over every little thing I’ve ever done wrong, or could’ve done wrong. Especially with the patients I’ve taken care of. I’ll think about something small, like if I didn’t check on somebody fast enough, or if I sounded irritated when I shouldn’t have, or if I missed something I should’ve noticed. And then it turns into this whole thing in my head where I’m not just someone who made a mistake, I’m a bad aide. Like I shouldn’t be trusted to take care of people.

And it’s not only work. I do it with my family too. I think about ways I should’ve helped more, or protected people better, or been more patient, or done something different. I keep replaying things and feeling like I failed them. Like I’m just this burden or this disappointment, and people would be better off if I wasn’t causing problems or needing anything.

And… I don’t know how to explain this without sounding strange, but sometimes it feels bigger than just me feeling guilty. It feels like God is mad at me. Like He sees all the ways I didn’t protect people right, or didn’t do enough, and He’s angry with me for it. I know people might say I’m being too hard on myself, but it feels real when I’m in it. It feels like I deserve to feel this bad because I didn’t do enough.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a traumatic event in your past?

I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think there’s one big traumatic event I can point to, like something obvious that happened to me where I’d say, “Yes, that’s the thing.” Nothing like that is coming to mind right now.

I mean, I’ve had hard things happen, and I’ve seen upsetting things at work sometimes, just because taking care of people can be a lot, but I don’t know if I would call it trauma. I guess I don’t really know where the line is. Some things stick with me more than I want them to, but I don’t have one specific event that I’ve been thinking of as traumatic.
Do you ever have memories or images from your past that feel very vivid and real, like they're happening again?

I don’t think so… not like it’s happening again, no.

I mean, I do think about things from the past a lot, probably too much, and sometimes I get stuck replaying things in my head, like what I should’ve done differently or whether I messed something up. But it feels more like remembering or worrying, if that makes sense. It doesn’t feel like I’m back there or like I’m seeing it like a movie in front of me.

I don’t really get vivid images where I lose track of where I am or anything like that. Sometimes a memory can feel emotionally strong, like it bothers me more than I think it should, but I still know I’m here and that it’s just me thinking about it. So… no, I don’t think I have memories that feel like they’re literally happening again.
Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're reliving a past experience, even if it's not necessarily traumatic?

I don’t think so… I mean, I can get really caught up thinking about things, like going over them again and again in my head, but I don’t know if I’d call it reliving.

Like, if I remember something I feel bad about, I might sit there and replay what I said or what I did, and I can get upset all over again. Sometimes it feels like my whole mood drops from just thinking about it. But I still know I’m here. I’m not suddenly back in that moment, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like my brain won’t let it go, not like I’m actually there again.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed moments where it feels like I’m reliving something. More like I’m stuck remembering and picking it apart.
Do you have trouble focusing on tasks or activities when you're awake?

I don’t know… I mean, I probably do sometimes, but I’m not sure what counts as trouble focusing.

Like, I can start something and then realize I’ve been sitting there not really doing it, or I’ll read the same thing over and over and it doesn’t stick. But then other times I can get through things if I really have to, especially if someone’s depending on me or it’s something right in front of me. So I don’t know if it’s focus exactly, or if it’s just that my mind feels tired and kind of… slow.

When I’m awake, it’s not like I’m always distracted by outside things. It’s more like I’ll try to pay attention and my thoughts sort of drift off, or I lose the thread of what I was doing. Even simple stuff can take longer because I have to keep reminding myself, “Okay, what was I doing?” But I haven’t really kept track of it or anything, so I’m not sure how bad it is.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on things when you're awake and trying to do something?

Yeah… I guess I do, but it’s hard for me to say how much is “hard to concentrate” and how much is just me feeling worn out or slow.

Like if I’m trying to do something, I can be looking right at it and still not really taking it in. I’ll start a task and then kind of stop, not because I decided to, but because my mind just drifts or gets blank. Then I’m like, wait, what was I just doing? Even little things can feel like they take more effort than they should. Reading is like that too sometimes—I’ll read the same line a bunch of times and realize I have no idea what I just read.

But I don’t know… I can still sometimes push through if I have to. So I’m not sure if I’d say I can’t concentrate, exactly. It’s more like staying with something takes a lot more work than it used to, and I don’t always trust my mind to stay on track.
Is there something specific at work or in your personal life that you think might be contributing to your sleep problems?

I think work is part of it, yeah… I mean, I work overnight, so my sleep is already kind of upside down, but lately it’s not just that. I’ll get off my shift and I’m exhausted, like my body should just shut down, and then I get home and lie there wide awake. I’ll be staring at the ceiling, hearing every little sound, and it feels like my mind just won’t settle.

And then when I finally do drift off, it’s not like real sleep. I wake up scared sometimes, like my heart is already going, and I don’t even feel like I rested. It’s broken up, like I’m in and out of it, and then I’m just lying there again trying to make myself sleep because I know I have to function later. So… I don’t know if it’s one specific thing in my personal life, but the overnight schedule and just not being able to calm down after it, that seems like a big part of why I came in.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or interest in activities you used to enjoy?

I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean… appetite, I haven’t been paying close attention to it like that. Some days I eat because I know I should, or because it’s just time, and other days I don’t really think about food until later. But I can’t say for sure that it’s a big change, because my schedule is weird anyway, with working nights and sleeping at odd times. So it’s hard to tell what’s actually different and what’s just me being off schedule.

And with things I used to enjoy… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really thought of it as “not enjoying” them, exactly. It’s more like I don’t always get around to doing things, or I’ll think about doing something and then it feels like too much effort to start. But I’m not sure if that counts. Like, I can’t point to one thing and say, “I used to love this and now I feel nothing.” It’s just kind of blurry.

So… maybe, but I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed it in a clear way, if that makes sense.

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I can't keep up with my care visits safely anymore, and my supervisor had to stop me during a care-plan visit because I was too overwhelmed and stuck to finish it. I've also pulled away from church, Zumba, and mentoring because I can barely manage work and getting home.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes. That’s actually been one of the bigger things, I think. I used to have more of a routine outside of just work and going home, and now it feels like everything has kind of narrowed down to just trying to make it through the day.

I used to go to church more, and that used to feel like something that kept me connected to people. I wasn’t always super involved every single week, but I went, and I knew people there, and it felt like a place I could show up. Lately I just… I don’t go. It feels like too much to get myself together and be around everyone, and then I feel bad because I know people probably notice, or maybe they don’t, I don’t know. But I’ve pulled back from that.

And Zumba too. I used to like that, even if I wasn’t great at it. It was something fun, something where I could move around and not think so much. But I haven’t been going. I tell myself I’m too tired, or I’ll go next time, but then next time comes and I still don’t. It just feels impossible to add anything extra when I’m already barely handling work.

I was mentoring too, and I’ve backed away from that. That one makes me feel really guilty, because it’s not just me missing a class or something. It’s like I was supposed to be there for somebody, and now I can barely be there for myself. I just get home and I’m done. I don’t have anything left in me.

Even work has gotten hard in a way that scares me, because I’m a personal care aide, so I have to be present and careful with people. And lately I can’t keep up with my care visits the way I should. I don’t feel like I can do them safely anymore sometimes. My supervisor actually had to stop me during a care-plan visit because I got so overwhelmed and stuck that I couldn’t finish it. I was just standing there, or trying to push through, but I couldn’t get my thoughts together enough to do what I was supposed to do.

So… yeah, it’s not just that I stopped doing fun things. It feels like I’ve stopped everything except the bare minimum, and even the bare minimum is starting to feel like too much.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant guilt or shame
doctor.question: Do you often feel guilty or ashamed about things you've done or haven't done?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with patients or my family, and it feels like I'm a worthless aide and God is mad at me for not protecting people better.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about guilt or shame over things done or not done, which directly matches excessive guilt and worthlessness.

patient.answer:
Yes… all the time. It’s like my mind won’t leave it alone. I keep going back over every little thing I’ve done wrong, or think I did wrong, even small things that maybe other people wouldn’t even remember. With patients, especially, I’ll think, did I miss something, did I say the wrong thing, did I not protect them the way I should have, did I rush, did I fail them somehow. And then I’ll replay it over and over until it feels bigger and bigger.

And with my family too. I think about all the ways I haven’t been there enough, or how I should have done more, or been stronger, or paid better attention. It doesn’t really stop at one mistake. It turns into this feeling like maybe I’m just… not good. Like I’m a worthless aide, and not really useful to anybody.

And I feel ashamed saying that because I know people might tell me I’m being too hard on myself, but it doesn’t feel that way inside. It feels true when I’m thinking it. Like God is mad at me too, like I didn’t protect people better, like I was supposed to do more and I failed. I keep asking myself why I couldn’t just do things right. It’s exhausting, but I can’t seem to let it go.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant weight loss or gain

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about recent weight changes, but the provided symptom profile does not include an appetite or weight-change symptom item.

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track, like I haven’t weighed myself regularly or anything. My clothes… I don’t know, they maybe feel about the same? I haven’t noticed anything really dramatic where I’d say, “Oh, I lost a lot,” or “I gained a lot.”

I guess with how things have been, I’m not paying close attention to my body like that. I just kind of get dressed and try to get through the day. So if there has been a change, I don’t know that I could say for sure. Nothing obvious that I’ve noticed, though.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's sleep disturbances are related to a specific traumatic event or stressor
doctor.question: Is there something specific that you think might have triggered your sleep problems, even if it doesn't feel directly related to a traumatic event?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance

patient.answer:
I don’t know if there was one specific thing that set it off. It’s not like I can point to one night and say, “That’s when it started,” or like it was because of one clear traumatic thing. It just… my sleep got broken up, and now it feels like I can’t get it back to normal.

A lot of it happens after my overnight shifts. I’ll get off work exhausted, like my body should just shut down, but then I get home and I’m lying there wide awake. I’ll be tired, but my mind won’t settle, and I’ll just stare or turn over and over. Then if I finally do drift off, it doesn’t feel peaceful. I wake up scared sometimes, like my body is already on alert before I even know why. And then after that I don’t feel rested at all, even if technically I slept some.

That’s honestly part of why I came in, because it’s not just “I had a bad night of sleep.” It’s like my sleep doesn’t work right anymore. I’m either awake when I should be sleeping, or I’m waking up frightened, or I get up feeling like I never really rested in the first place. So I don’t know what triggered it exactly… I just know it’s been happening and it’s wearing me down.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of dissociative symptoms
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself from somewhere else?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about depersonalization or dissociation, specifically feeling outside the body and watching oneself. This symptom is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying, I don’t think. Like, I’ve heard people describe that as watching themselves from above or feeling like they’re not in their own body, and I can’t really say that’s happened to me.

Sometimes I feel kind of distant or not fully present, especially when I’m worn down, but I still feel like I’m me, inside my own body. I’m not looking at myself from somewhere else. It’s more like I’m tired or foggy and trying to get through the moment, if that makes sense. But no, I don’t think I’ve had that outside-my-body feeling.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has feelings of worthlessness
doctor.question: Do you often feel worthless or like you're a burden to others?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with patients or my family, and it feels like I'm a worthless aide and God is mad at me for not protecting people better.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about feelings of worthlessness or being a burden to others, which matches this symptom item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I do. A lot. Probably more than I want to admit.

It’s like my mind just keeps going back over every little thing I’ve ever done wrong, or could’ve done wrong. Especially with the patients I’ve taken care of. I’ll think about something small, like if I didn’t check on somebody fast enough, or if I sounded irritated when I shouldn’t have, or if I missed something I should’ve noticed. And then it turns into this whole thing in my head where I’m not just someone who made a mistake, I’m a bad aide. Like I shouldn’t be trusted to take care of people.

And it’s not only work. I do it with my family too. I think about ways I should’ve helped more, or protected people better, or been more patient, or done something different. I keep replaying things and feeling like I failed them. Like I’m just this burden or this disappointment, and people would be better off if I wasn’t causing problems or needing anything.

And… I don’t know how to explain this without sounding strange, but sometimes it feels bigger than just me feeling guilty. It feels like God is mad at me. Like He sees all the ways I didn’t protect people right, or didn’t do enough, and He’s angry with me for it. I know people might say I’m being too hard on myself, but it feels real when I’m in it. It feels like I deserve to feel this bad because I didn’t do enough.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of traumatic events

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about past traumatic experiences, but the provided symptom profile does not include a trauma history item.

patient.answer:
I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think there’s one big traumatic event I can point to, like something obvious that happened to me where I’d say, “Yes, that’s the thing.” Nothing like that is coming to mind right now.

I mean, I’ve had hard things happen, and I’ve seen upsetting things at work sometimes, just because taking care of people can be a lot, but I don’t know if I would call it trauma. I guess I don’t really know where the line is. Some things stick with me more than I want them to, but I don’t have one specific event that I’ve been thinking of as traumatic.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of experiencing flashbacks
doctor.question: Do you ever have memories or images from your past that feel very vivid and real, like they're happening again?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about vivid re-experiencing memories or flashbacks from the past, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not like it’s happening again, no.

I mean, I do think about things from the past a lot, probably too much, and sometimes I get stuck replaying things in my head, like what I should’ve done differently or whether I messed something up. But it feels more like remembering or worrying, if that makes sense. It doesn’t feel like I’m back there or like I’m seeing it like a movie in front of me.

I don’t really get vivid images where I lose track of where I am or anything like that. Sometimes a memory can feel emotionally strong, like it bothers me more than I think it should, but I still know I’m here and that it’s just me thinking about it. So… no, I don’t think I have memories that feel like they’re literally happening again.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of experiencing flashbacks
doctor.question: Do you ever have moments where you feel like you're reliving a past experience, even if it's not necessarily traumatic?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reliving past experiences or flashback-like experiences, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… I mean, I can get really caught up thinking about things, like going over them again and again in my head, but I don’t know if I’d call it reliving.

Like, if I remember something I feel bad about, I might sit there and replay what I said or what I did, and I can get upset all over again. Sometimes it feels like my whole mood drops from just thinking about it. But I still know I’m here. I’m not suddenly back in that moment, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like my brain won’t let it go, not like I’m actually there again.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed moments where it feels like I’m reliving something. More like I’m stuck remembering and picking it apart.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has difficulty concentrating

target_item.reason: The question is directly about concentration or difficulty focusing while awake, and the provided symptom profile does not include a concentration/attention symptom item.

I don’t know… I mean, I probably do sometimes, but I’m not sure what counts as trouble focusing.

Like, I can start something and then realize I’ve been sitting there not really doing it, or I’ll read the same thing over and over and it doesn’t stick. But then other times I can get through things if I really have to, especially if someone’s depending on me or it’s something right in front of me. So I don’t know if it’s focus exactly, or if it’s just that my mind feels tired and kind of… slow.

When I’m awake, it’s not like I’m always distracted by outside things. It’s more like I’ll try to pay attention and my thoughts sort of drift off, or I lose the thread of what I was doing. Even simple stuff can take longer because I have to keep reminding myself, “Okay, what was I doing?” But I haven’t really kept track of it or anything, so I’m not sure how bad it is.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has difficulty concentrating due to their current mental state
doctor.question: Do you find it hard to concentrate on things when you're awake and trying to do something?

target_item.reason: The question is directly about difficulty concentrating while awake, but the provided symptom profiles do not include a concentration or attention symptom item.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess I do, but it’s hard for me to say how much is “hard to concentrate” and how much is just me feeling worn out or slow.

Like if I’m trying to do something, I can be looking right at it and still not really taking it in. I’ll start a task and then kind of stop, not because I decided to, but because my mind just drifts or gets blank. Then I’m like, wait, what was I just doing? Even little things can feel like they take more effort than they should. Reading is like that too sometimes—I’ll read the same line a bunch of times and realize I have no idea what I just read.

But I don’t know… I can still sometimes push through if I have to. So I’m not sure if I’d say I can’t concentrate, exactly. It’s more like staying with something takes a lot more work than it used to, and I don’t always trust my mind to stay on track.

I’ll be staring at the ceiling, hearing every little sound, and it feels like my mind just won’t settle.

It’s broken up, like I’m in and out of it, and then I’m just lying there again trying to make myself sleep because I know I have to function later. So… I don’t know if it’s one specific thing in my personal life, but the overnight schedule and just not being able to calm down after it, that seems like a big part of why I came in.
